newsitem.title: CANADA: Ottawa meeting finally launches Zaire mission.
newsitem.headline: Ottawa meeting finally launches Zaire mission.

text.p: Ambassadors of a dozen nations on Friday formally approved the launch of a scaled-down mission to help refugees in eastern Zaire, the Canadian chairman of the meeting said.
"Now the multinational force is formally constituted," Canadian Assistant Deputy Foreign Minister Paul Heinbecker told reporters after heading the meeting.

The authorization came nearly three weeks after Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien telephoned world leaders seeking help to rescue what aid agencies said were more than a million refugees and displaced people in eastern Zaire.
Since then about 600,000 refugees have returned to Rwanda, but Western officials have identified at least 200,000 more and believe there could be hundreds of thousands of others.

"Reports of continued human suffering indicate we need to be prepared if more help is needed," Canadian Foreign Minister Lloyd Axworthy said on Thursday afternoon as he announced agreement from more than 20 countries to go ahead.

Controversy has surrounded the plan to airdrop supplies to the refugees, partly because of the reluctance of the Rwandan government to allow a military force to operate from Rwanda or for humanitarian agencies to cross into Zaire from Rwanda.
